head: 98ca9a7526ca77c1bd76a8e24b318589c19579ef
summary:
Build attempt 2 (98ca9a7) makes the three accepted fixes, and nothing else, in docs/design/SL-068-sort-on-read.md:
- **m1:** the brief's 9-40 ms is now traced to SL-042's reflection.
- **m2:** "nothing is kept per folder" is said of the store only, and the window's kept Children arrays are named in both the Memory bullet and Not covered.
- **R2-m3:** the reversal is priced against what is left of the budget, 136 MiB less SL-042's 96 MiB.

It also adds two checks to C-004 in tests/bugs/SL-068-DecisionCases.ps1.

I checked every new citation against its source:
- reflect-1.json:74 reads 'measured 9-40 ms against 250 ms'.
- validate-slice-1.json has '9.16–9.80 ms', with an en dash, which is what the new check looks for.
- reflect-1.json:84 gives the 136 MiB and the 96 MiB, and 652.1 − 555.8 = 96.3 at SL-042 doc :82-84.
- FolderTreeNode.cs:14-16 says 'kept until the next scan'. This backs the builder's declared wording change.
- FolderTreeNode.cs:142-158 stores `Children = nodes` and returns early on later opens.

Nothing else moved. The SL-042 doc, src/, the test projects and .taad/fitness.yaml are untouched since attempt 1, so the dotnet and T-003 results from attempt 1 still apply.

The new text does not trip the existing C-004 regexes:
- '35.9-40.2' now breaks before 'ms', and in any case starts above 20, so the merged-range check ignores it.
- '9.16-9.80' does not match the '9-40' pattern.

`SL-068-DecisionCases.ps1 -Case All`: exit 0, every check held, including the two new C-004 checks. Nothing new departed from the design.

Second round: Nothing new in this round. Attempt 2 adds three readers to C-004 (tests/bugs/SL-068-DecisionCases.ps1:290-294), and I tried to break each one. Every input the formats allow either still reads correctly or makes the check fail. None lets it pass silently.

- **Line 74 of reflect-1.json:** read by Read-Tree, so CRLF becomes LF and a BOM is dropped. If the JSON were reformatted, the line moves and the check fails; it cannot pass by accident.
- **Validate record:** matched on the raw text '9.16–9.80 ms', en dash as the file stores it today. If the dash were written as the escape – or the file were removed, the check fails or throws. The script runs with ErrorAction Stop, so it exits non-zero either way.
- **Origin sentence:** matched after Flat collapses whitespace, so the doc's line break between '35.9-40.2' and 'ms' reads as one space. The new check therefore passes on the real text and still failed on the builder's mutant.

The new doc text also leaves the existing regexes alone:
- '9.16-9.80 ms' matches the merged-range pattern, but it is not flagged, because its upper bound, 9.80, is not above 45.
- No new line matches the '9-40' pattern except the one that also says 'brief'.

`-Case All` exits 0.

obligations.evidence: docs/design/SL-068-sort-on-read.md:42-45 now reads: 'The slice's brief says 9-40 ms, taken from SL-042's reflection (.taad/slices/SL-042/reflect-1.json:74), which joined SL-042's validate run (9.16-9.80 ms, .taad/slices/SL-042/validate-slice-1.json) and its build run (35.9-40.2 ms). The runs above reach 44.12, so this record quotes 9-44.' The sources match. SL-068-DecisionCases.ps1:290-294 asserts the sentence and both sources, and passed when I ran it.

docs/design/SL-068-sort-on-read.md:60-63 now reads 'Nothing is kept per folder in the store; the folder tree keeps the rows it built for each folder it has opened, in that order, until the session ends at the next scan (FolderTreeNode.cs:14-16 and :142-158)'. Not covered at :84-85 names `FolderTreeNode.Children` as the ordered copy a refresh would have to invalidate. I confirmed both against FolderTreeNode.cs:14-16 ('kept until the next scan') and EnsureChildren.

docs/design/SL-068-sort-on-read.md:73-76 now reads 'paid out of what is left of the memory budget (the earlier spike's layout had about 136 MiB of headroom, of which SL-042 then spent 96 MiB retained, .taad/slices/SL-042/reflect-1.json:84)'. That is the accepted wording and it matches the reflection's line 84.
'The rule, and who wrote it' is unchanged since attempt 1. C-005 still passes: git puts the rule and the result in the same commit, b5c2b62, and the ledger dates the design first.
The timing test, the csproj filter and the build configuration are all unchanged since attempt 1, when my default run showed the test ran as 'Debug build'. C-006 still passes.
The submitted-text section is unchanged and still says 'not applied'. C-001 passes.
The find/replace blocks are unchanged. C-002 passes.
The SL-042 doc is unchanged since attempt 1. C-003 passes, reading numstat 2 0 against 6566536.
The listed reads, the range and the harness items are unchanged, and the brief's origin is now correct (O-011). C-004 passes, including its two new checks.
'What reopens it' is unchanged. C-006 passes.
The Not covered live-refresh item keeps SL-044's 84 ms against 50 and its citation, and now also names the window's kept arrays. C-007 passes.
The attempt 2 diff touches only docs/design/SL-068-sort-on-read.md, tests/bugs/SL-068-DecisionCases.ps1 and .taad/slices/SL-068/*. C-008 passes.

cases.evidence: SL-068-DecisionCases.ps1:290-294 now reads reflect-1.json line 74 and validate-slice-1.json, and asserts that the record's origin sentence names both SL-042 runs. The builder restored the old 'rounded this' sentence and C-004 failed. That closes the gap m1 found in the earlier check at :288-289.

drift: Nothing new departed from the design in attempt 2. The one wording change, 'until the session ends at the next scan' where the accepted fix said 'until the session ends', was declared and matches FolderTreeNode.cs:16.
unreviewed: .taad/slices/SL-068/*.json (index, build-slice-1/2, code-review-1, validate-slice-1): engine ledger records, not slice code.
